newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices soften as June flows begin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices soften as June flows begin.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices started the month on the defensive Monday, pressured by fairly mild weather over much of the nation and forecasts for more of the same through the week, industry sources said.
While many expected the cash to stumble early in the month, few expected prices to crater, counting on prospects for broader cooling loads later to temper the bears.

"It's not a freefall. There's still no real (hot) weather, but I think we'll see the $2.30s again when it arrives," said one Midwest trader, noting early-June Louisiana Gulf prices were talked about four cents lower in the mid-to-high teens.
The one relatively bright spot for the bulls was the West, where hot weather there limited losses to only a couple of cents in west Texas and in southern California.
Gas on El Paso Permian was quoted in the $2.01-05 area, while southern California border gas was pegged at $2.15-2.20.
Below-normal temperatures in south Texas pressured prices down several cents to the $2.10 area.

And in the Midwest, where temperatures also remained below normal, June prices on pipelines like Panhandle softened two to three cents to the low-$2s. Chicago city gate gas slipped several cents to the mid-$2.20s.

In the East, New York city gate prices held relatively steady in the mid-$2.40s despite forecasts for slightly below-normal weather through the week. But Appalachian gas eased a couple of cents to the mid-to-high $2.30s.
